proposed_core_edits.proposed: The target is \(\tau_P(x_0)\) at a fixed known \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\). Under consistency and conditional exchangeability, \(\tau_P=\mu_{1,P}-\mu_{0,P}\) is a version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X]\); H\"older continuity and exact-uniform full support determine its unique continuous version at every fixed interior or boundary \(x_0\), cf. KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives a lower bound on a broader bounded-density pointwise CATE class, while Theorem 2 gives an upper bound under additional design and nuisance-estimation conditions; the displayed lower hard laws use separated local support.
Theorem 2.1 bounds the affinity of two convex mixtures of product measures under a measurable partition and coordinate-local perturbations.
Theorems 3--5 establish matched local and global conditional-variance rates under random design using local U-statistics and coupled lower laws.
Theorem 3 and Corollary 4 give local-polynomial R-learner upper rates with deterministic smoothness-dependent tuning under known-density conditions.

project_justification.gap: The published pointwise CATE theory gives this candidate power on a broader model, but its displayed lower laws delete design mass around nuisance-bump transitions. A lower bound on that broader class does not imply the same bound after fixing \(P_X\) to the exact uniform law, and it does not by itself certify arbitrary boundary or interior point targets on the singleton class.
project_justification.niche: The note isolates the exact known-uniform, bounded-overlap Bernoulli/interiority subclass and proves its pointwise estimation/precision benchmark. The class is a strict subclass of the published general-design model, so a same-class converse is the missing ingredient; identification is already supplied by consistency, exchangeability, overlap, full support, and continuity.
project_justification.fill: A reflected inward chart gives one total finite projection \(U\)-statistic estimator uniformly over fixed \(x_0\). For the converse, a translated compact smooth window and squared frame partition make singleton sign mixtures agree exactly; sparse component factorization, a mixed-amplitude Hellinger bound, and spanning-tree enumeration control the full fixed-\(n\) mixture. At equality, \(n\ell^d\) is a tunably small constant, which closes the elbow without a logarithm.
